input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition was inverted to `not any_prefix_is_slash` when moving the code into get_help_spec. The original code used `"; "` for slash-prefixed options and `" / "` otherwise, so the new code swaps them for every option.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with secondary spellings and no slash prefix, such as `--shout/--no-shout`. Originally any_prefix_is_slash is False, so the separator was " / ". The new expression evaluates to "; ", so get_help_record now returns "--shout; --no-shout" instead of "--shout / --no-shout". Impact: the help output for the common boolean-flag case changes, and existing help-output tests for those options would fail. The intended behavior change in the commit title is about hidden options, not separators.
critique: The finding identifies the same inverted `not any_prefix_is_slash` condition that swaps the separators. It gives the same `--shout; --no-shout` failure, so the mechanism and failure path match the label.
